title: [04/01/2025] Donation given to six different types of charity
prompt: The chart below shows the donation given to six different types of charity by one company from 2012 to 2014 (in millions). Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the amounts of money donated to six different types of charity by one company over a three-year period from 2012 to 2014.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the donation patterns varied significantly across different charity types during this period, with some categories experiencing increases while others showed declining trends. Social welfare consistently received the highest donations throughout the period, whereas arts received the least funding across all three years.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the categories that received higher levels of funding, social welfare was the most generously supported charity in 2012, receiving approximately 22 million, which was significantly higher than education at around 7.5 million and health at roughly 5.5 million. By 2014, social welfare donations had increased to about 24 million after experiencing a decline to 16 million in 2013, maintaining its position as the largest recipient. In contrast, health funding showed a steady upward trend, rising to approximately 8.5 million in the final year, while education experienced fluctuation, dropping to around 5.5 million in 2013 before recovering to its original level of 7.5 million by 2014.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining charity types, environment received about 7.5 million in 2012, which was similar to education, while wildlife and arts attracted considerably less support at approximately 2.5 million each. Environment donations fluctuated throughout the period, dropping to roughly 4.5 million in 2013 before recovering slightly to 6.5 million in 2014. Wildlife funding showed consistent growth, rising from 2.5 million in 2012 to 3 million in 2013 and reaching 4.5 million by 2014, whereas arts remained consistently low across all three years, staying at around 2.5-3 million throughout the period.
